1  For Petitioner : Mr.M.Gnana Gurunathan  For R1 & R2 : Mr.M.Senthil Ayyanar  Government Advocate  For R3 : Mrs.S.Devasena  Standing Counsel  ORDER This writ petition has been filed challenging the order, dated 03.10.2024 passed by the second respondent, thereby, sealed the petitioner's premises. 
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials placed before this Court.
3. The petitioner owned a premises at Flat No.A8/1, admeasuring 925 sq.ft in ground floor in Block No.A8 in Re-survey No.161/1A Part & 168/8 situated at Madurai Corporation Ward No.44,
M.I.G.Colony, K.K.Nagar, Madurai. In front of his house, he has a petty shop and one Sivakumar is taking care of the petty shop. While being so, FIR, in Cr.No.622/2024, on the file of the Inspector of Police, Anna Nagar Police Station, Madurai, has been registered as against him alleging that he sells banned tobacco products and thereafter, the shop was sealed. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is not selling any food products. He is selling only the STASH Pro Rolling Paper for the purpose of packaging the food. 
Except this material, no other food products or Tobacco are selling in the petty shop. Therefore, the respondents have no jurisdiction to lock and seal the premises. That apart, the lock and seal was ordered without even mentioning the period. After registration of FIR, no complaint has been filed by the respondents before the Adjudicating authority to prosecute the petitioner. 
5. On perusal of the records revealed that the FIR was registered as against one Sivakumar and the Lock and Seal was also passed only against the Sivakumar. The petitioner claims to be a owner of the premises and filed this writ petition. The said Sivakumar did not file any petition sofar. 
However, the premises was sealed without mentioning any period. That apart, sofar, no prosecution has been initiated as against the said Sivakumar. 
6. In view of the above, the third respondent is directed to initiate the prosecution as against the said Sivakumar and proceed further in the manner known to law within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Keerthikumar vs The Commissioner on 22 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149924696/
2 7. The petitioner is directed to submit a representation to the second respondent in order to remove the lock and seal and on receipt of the same, the second respondent is directed to consider the representation of the petitioner to remove the lock and seal and pass orders in the manner known law within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the representation. 
8. With the above direction, the writ petition stands disposed of. No costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
